theater: 不列顛東南部（肯特與泰晤士河）

battle.name: 羅馬征服不列顛
battle.theater: 不列顛東南部（肯特與泰晤士河）
battle.brief: 公元43年夏，帝國以第二奧古斯塔、第十四孳生、第十瓦萊里亞三個軍團渡海入不列顛，連戰肯特、兩渡泰晤士河，入據卡穆羅杜努姆，翌年卡西維拉努斯出降。卡面科林斯青銅盔是希臘式樣，公元前六百五十年已定型，四十三年只餘工藝血統：羅軍戴的是開放面罩的科魯斯與蒙特福提諾型青銅盔。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 公元四十三年的不列顛遠征，是羅馬帝國與不列顛諸部族聯盟之間一場極不對稱的戰爭。羅馬一方由皇帝克勞狄烏斯親自主導，但真正掛名統兵的是兩位禁衛軍長（praetorian prefect）納西斯與帕拉斯：納西斯奉命督管海軍與登陸後勤，帕拉斯隨軍統轄三個軍團，兩人都以皇帝私人代表的身份介入海外戰役，這在共和以來從無先例。野戰全權交給帝國總督普勞提烏斯，其下是三個帝國軍團的指揮官：維斯帕申領第二奧古斯塔軍團，科爾布羅領第十四孳生軍團，蘇埃托尼烏斯·保利努斯領第十瓦萊里亞·維克托里克斯軍團。輔助軍才是遠征的骨幹：巴達維人的騎兵大隊在兩次河流戰役中都扮演關鍵角色，另有巴達維與通格里亞的步兵大隊、數個騎兵大隊與輔助步兵中隊，以及隨軍的工兵營造隊。不列顛南部並非全無羅馬助力：阿特里巴特斯王國的曼杜布拉基烏斯與雷格納王國的科吉杜姆努斯願意接受羅馬保護、替帝國引路，前者的都城卡穆羅杜努姆更被選為羅馬殖民地的落點。反過來，抵抗方沒有中央政權，是由卡圖維拉尼人、廷杜桑提人、伊契尼人與肯特諸部組成的鬆散聯盟，戰時由國王卡西維拉努斯實際指揮，部落首領各自帶兵，戰力與配合全看各人。
countriesEn: The invasion of Britain in AD 43 was an extremely lopsided war between the Roman Empire and an alliance of British tribes. On the Roman side the emperor Claudius drove the enterprise, but the command in the field was nominally in the hands of two praetorian prefects, Narcissus and Pallas: Narcissus was given charge of the fleet and of the logistics of the landings, Pallas travelled with the army and supervised the three legions, and both of them intervened in an overseas war as personal representatives of the emperor, a pattern without precedent since the Republic. Full operational command was delegated to the provincial governor Aulus Plautius, under whom served the commanders of the three citizen legions: Vespasian with Legio II Augusta, Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo with Legio XIV Gemina, and Gaius Suetonius Paulinus with Legio XX Valeria Victrix. The auxiliaries, not the legions, formed the backbone of the expedition: a Batavian cavalry ala was decisive in both of the river fights, and there were Batavian and Tungrian infantry cohorts, several further alae and auxiliary infantry units, together with the engineers who built the bridge. Southern Britain was not without Roman friends: Mandubracius of the Atrebates and Cogidumnus of the Regni were willing to accept Roman protection and to guide the empire, and the former's capital, Camulodunum, was chosen as the site of a Roman colony. The other side had no central government at all, but a loose league of the Catuvellauni, Trinovantes, Iceni and the tribes of Kent, commanded in the field by King Cassivellaunus, with every warband led by its own chief and cohesion depending entirely on personal loyalties.
people: 這場戰爭留下的人名，大半出自《克勞狄烏斯傳》與卡西烏斯·狄奧的編年，而不是戰場本身。皇帝克勞狄烏斯是整場行動的政治推手：他在四三年春於法國魯昂遇刺，刺客是不列顛人，供詞指向皇帝近侍納西斯；受驚之餘，他同意遠征，並把指揮權交給近侍與將領，自己直到戰局大致底定才登上島嶼。總督普勞提烏斯率軍渡海後指揮最初的戰鬥，卻在倫敦一役後元氣大傷，兵鋒為之鈍化，連卡穆羅杜努姆的鎮守也幾乎失控。維斯帕申是全軍最耀眼的名字：他在第二奧古斯塔軍團身先士卒，據蘇埃托尼烏斯記載，他的肩部中了一箭，劇痛延續數日才消退，傷癒之後又立新功，後來成為皇帝。科爾布羅領第十四孳生軍團，穩住左翼；保利努斯領第十瓦萊里亞·維克托里克斯軍團，在肯特前線承受了最艱難的攻擊。敵方以卡西維拉努斯最關鍵，這位卡圖維拉尼人的國王在金幣上留下自己的名字，並在倫敦一役受挫後仍重整兵馬，最終赴卡穆羅杜努姆向皇帝歸降。伊契尼人國王庫諾貝利努斯選擇服從並送出人質，曼杜布拉基烏斯與科吉杜姆努斯則以附庸王的身份周旋其間。同期身在羅馬的奧維德於流放地寫下《漁業論》，恰好提到不列顛的船與北方海域的魚，時間與這場遠征重合。
peopleEn: Almost all the names this war has left us come from the Life of Claudius and from the chronicles of Cassius Dio rather than from the battlefield itself. The emperor Claudius was the political engine of the whole operation: in the spring of AD 43 he was attacked at Rouen in Gaul by a British assassin whose testimony pointed at the imperial intimate Narcissus, and, shaken by it, he agreed to the invasion and handed the conduct of it to his freedmen and his generals, boarding the island himself only when the outcome was largely settled. The governor Aulus Plautius led the crossing and directed the opening fighting, but the reverses in the fighting on the Thames blunted the army, and the holding of Camulodunum nearly slipped out of his hands. Vespasian was the most conspicuous figure in the army: he led the Second Augustan in person, and according to Suetonius an arrow struck his shoulder in the fighting, the pain lasting for several days before it subsided, and he went on to add fresh distinction to his name before becoming emperor himself. Corbulo commanded the Fourteenth Gemini and steadied the left; Paulinus commanded the Twentieth Valeria Victrix and bore the hardest of the attacks on the Kentish front. On the other side the key figure was Cassivellaunus, king of the Catuvellauni, who put his own name on his gold coin and, after being checked on the Thames, re-raised his forces and finally came to Camulodunum to surrender to the emperor. Cunobelinus, king of the Iceni, chose submission and sent hostages; Mandubracius and Cogidumnus moved between the two sides in the role of client kings. In Rome at the same time the poet Ovid, in his exile, was writing the Halieutica, in which the ships of Britain and the fish of the northern sea appear, at almost exactly the moment of this expedition.
kits: 本卡的科林斯青銅盔是希臘作風的重裝頭盔：整片青銅包覆面部，只有眼孔與鼻脊留空，頭盔重達數公斤。它的代價正像卡面所寫——戴著它的人幾乎聽不見外界的聲音，視野只能向前，轉頭要靠整個身體；能撐住這種裝備的，只有緊密的隊形。可是在公元四十三年的不列顛，這種全封閉面罩的頭盔早已退出軍備數百年，羅馬軍團裝備的是開放面罩的青銅盔：科魯斯型與蒙特福提諾型，附有可活動的護頰與護頸，意大利北部的冶坊大量生產、經軍械官配發給輔助兵，肯特與泰晤士河沿岸的營地與墓葬考古都出土過這類頭盔。卡面這頂盔在戰役裡的位置，是工藝血統的源頭而不是實物：它的銅合金鑄造傳統一路演變成四十三年的開放式青銅盔，駐英的羅馬兵卒正是靠隊形、而不是靠視聽，維持住那條戰線。雙方其他裝備同樣懸殊。羅馬步兵持大曲盾（scutum）、半劍（gladius，約六十公分，刃部可刺可砍）、重標槍（pilum，槍桿約兩公尺，槍頭重逾一公斤），護身以鎖子甲（lorica hamata）為主——分段的板甲要到公元八十年代在萊茵河軍營才出現，四十三年尚未問世。輔助騎兵配圓盾與青銅護頰。英軍這邊，長鐵劍、長矛（可達三公尺）、帶金屬盾凸的圓盾、短弓與小圓盾都是常見配置，卻幾乎沒有護甲。攻城與工程方面，多塞特郡霍德山的堡壘出土過一枚羅馬攻城弩箭，年代落在公元四十三至五十一年之間；渡過泰晤士河的羅馬木橋，則在倫敦河底留下橋墩遺構。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on this card is a Greek heavy headpiece: a single sheet of bronze enclosing the whole face, with only eye slits and a nasal left open, and it weighed several kilograms. Its price is exactly what the card states: the man wearing it could barely hear the world outside, could see only straight ahead, and had to turn his whole body to look aside; the only thing that made such a burden supportable was a tight formation. By AD 43, however, the fully closed helmet had been out of service for several centuries, and the Roman legions wore open-faced bronze helmets instead, of Coolus and Montefortino type, with movable cheek pieces and neck guards, mass-produced in northern Italy and issued to the auxiliaries by the armourers; helmets of this kind have been excavated from camps and graves along the Kentish coast and the Thames. The place of the card's helmet in this campaign is therefore as the ancestor of a craft tradition rather than as an artefact on the field: its cast bronze lineage ran on into the open-faced helmets of AD 43, and it was formation, not sight and hearing, that kept the Roman line in Britain together. The rest of the equipment on both sides was just as uneven. Roman infantry carried the large curved scutum, the gladius about sixty centimetres long with a blade that could thrust and cut, and the heavy pilum, a javelin with a shaft of some two metres and a head of more than a kilogram, and they were protected mainly by mail, lorica hamata: the segmented plate armour, lorica segmentata, does not appear until the legionary camps on the Rhine in the eighties of the century and did not yet exist in AD 43. Auxiliary cavalry used round shields and bronze cheek pieces. On the British side the long iron sword, the long spear of up to three metres, the round shield with a metal boss, the short bow and the small round buckler were all common, but body armour was almost entirely absent. On the engineering side a Roman artillery bolt has been found at the hillfort of Hod Hill in Dorset, dated to between AD 43 and AD 51, and the Roman timber bridge that carried the army over the Thames survives as pier remains in the river bed at London.
tactics: 羅馬軍隊在島上全程以行軍營（castra）為依托宿營，每夜挖壕樹柵、結營而臥，營地形制與朝向在肯特北部海岸線的考古中仍可辨認，說明遠征隊自登陸起就按戰役節奏移動，而不是散開劫掠。進攻序列沿用帝國軍團的標準三列：前排輕裝兵（velites）擲投標槍後退入兩翼，第二列的持槍步兵以密集陣形擲出重標槍（pilum），靠重量把敵方的長矛與盾壓歪，第三列持劍重步兵上前列陣格鬥；輔助步兵與騎兵在兩翼策應。渡河是關鍵。第一次在肯特某條河兩岸的交鋒，蘇埃托尼烏斯記得很清楚：不列顛人沿岸列陣，羅馬軍把巴達維騎兵扣在後方不用，直到近身戰打到僵持才放騎兵出擊，一擊扭轉局面。第二次是泰晤士河，羅馬人造橋架設，渡河後兩軍在林地與沼澤間激戰：不列顛人退入大片樹林，羅馬軍追入後遭四面反擊，陣形大亂，才改用龜甲陣（testudo）抵禦；戰事拖成兩日，羅馬軍損失慘重，終於迫使英軍放棄海岸。英軍的戰術全在地形與節奏上：狄奧記載他們把馬嘴用生皮纏住，逼近後即轉向，以長矛回刺騷擾羅馬騎兵，並用號角與呼號驚嚇羅馬馬匹，使帝國騎兵幾乎無法投入；他們也用車列結成壁壘阻擋羅馬步兵推進，並在林中設伏，趁羅馬軍深入而發動反擊。
tacticsEn: Throughout the campaign the Roman army lived in its marching camps, castra, digging a ditch, throwing up a rampart and closing the camp each night; the shape and alignment of those camps can still be read in the archaeology of the north Kentish coast, which shows that the expedition moved as a going operation from the moment of the landing rather than dispersing to plunder. The order of attack followed the standard three-line formation of the imperial legions: light troops, the velites, threw their missiles and withdrew to the flanks; the second line, the spearmen, delivered the heavy pilum in a dense formation, using its weight to bend the enemy's long spears and shields; the third line, the swordsmen, closed to hand fighting, with auxiliary infantry and cavalry working the flanks. The river crossings were the crux of the operation. In the first clash, on the banks of a river in Kent, Suetonius is explicit: the Britons were drawn up along the bank, and the Romans held the Batavian cavalry back from the fighting until the melee had locked, then let them go in, and a single charge decided the day. The second was the Thames, where the Romans built a bridge, crossed, and fought it out among woods and marshes: the Britons withdrew into a great forest, the Romans followed them in, were struck from several sides, saw their formations break up, and only then closed into a testudo; the business dragged on for two days, the Romans suffered heavily, and the British were finally driven from the coast. The British method was entirely a matter of ground and tempo: Dio records them muzzling their horses in raw hide, riding up and then wheeling away to prod the Roman cavalry with their long spears, and using horns and cries to frighten the Roman horses, so that the imperial cavalry could scarcely be brought into play; they also formed a barricade of their wagons to hold up the Roman infantry, and they used ambushes in the woods, striking the Romans after they had penetrated too far.
data: 這場戰爭留下的數字很少，卻值得逐條分清可靠與誇大。軍力方面，出征的是三個帝國軍團：第二奧古斯塔、第十四孳生與第十瓦萊里亞·維克托里克斯；帝國時期一個軍團的編制通常記在五千人上下，實際常駐往往低於此數，再加上一倍左右的輔助軍，一般估計遠征總兵力在四萬人上下。運輸方面，史料沒有留下可靠的船數，只能從編制反推艦隊以數十艘為量級。距離方面，從登陸地沿肯特海岸到泰晤士河約五六十公里，再北上面向卡穆羅杜努姆又約六十公里，一個作戰季節要走完全程。時間上，登陸與主要戰鬥集中在公元四十三年的夏季至初秋，皇帝本人於同年秋末抵達，凱旋典禮定於公元四十四年一月十七日舉行，羅馬的凱旋拱門則在公元五十一至五十二年落成。傷亡方面，卡西烏斯·狄奧在六十卷二十節記下一次交戰雙方各折損約二萬人——這幾乎肯定是誇大的數字，但它是這場戰爭唯一流傳下來的傷亡估算。工程方面，倫敦出土的羅馬橋墩遺構顯示那座泰晤士河木橋長度在二百五十至三百五十公尺之間，是當時已知最長的羅馬橋之一。
dataEn: Few figures survive for this war, and it is worth separating the reliable from the inflated. On strength: three citizen legions went out, the Second Augusta, the Fourteenth Gemini and the Twentieth Valeria Victrix. A legion of the early empire is normally reckoned at about five thousand men on paper, though the numbers actually billeted were usually lower, and to that must be added roughly an equal body of auxiliaries, giving a commonly estimated total for the expedition of around forty thousand men. On transport, no reliable count of ships survives, and the scale of the fleet can only be inferred from the establishment as a matter of tens of vessels. On distance: some fifty to sixty kilometres along the Kentish coast from the landing place to the Thames, and a further sixty kilometres northward to Camulodunum, the whole length of it to be covered within a single campaigning season. On time: the landing and the main fighting fall in the summer and early autumn of AD 43, the emperor himself arrived in the late autumn of the same year, his triumph was fixed for 17 January AD 44, and the arch in Rome was dedicated in AD 51 or 52. On losses: Cassius Dio, in book LX chapter 20, records about twenty thousand men falling on each side in a single engagement; the figure is almost certainly exaggerated, but it is the only casualty estimate this war has transmitted. On engineering: the remains of the Roman bridge piers recovered in London indicate a timber bridge across the Thames of between roughly two hundred and fifty and three hundred and fifty metres, one of the longest Roman bridges then known.
cause: 要理解四十三年的遠征，得從三條線一起看。第一是帝國北疆的形勢：萊茵河畔常駐的軍團無法抽調，而高盧北部在頭一年才剛平定，蠻族首領克諾多瑪留斯起事被壓下，帝國需要一條更安穩的西界。第二是南不列顛本身的王位糾葛：阿特里巴特斯王國的國王維里卡被自己的臣民驅逐，逃到高盧向羅馬求援；雷格納王國的科吉杜姆努斯之父維爾卡西維拉努斯更早就逃到羅馬，被帝國安置為附庸王。於是羅馬方面得以主張自己在南不列顛的既有權利，並以仲裁者身份介入。第三是皇帝本人的處境：四三年春在魯昂遇刺後，克勞狄烏斯需要一場勝仗來鞏固新得的權位，而納西斯與帕拉斯這批近侍也急需軍功；狄奧記錄皇帝最初提出的要求，是歸還流亡者與掠走的財物，卡西維拉努斯拒絕，戰爭由此爆發。至於經濟層面，征服還意味著掌握西南部的錫礦與鉛礦、以及不列顛與高盧之間的貿易通道，這是長期收益，遠征則是為它投下的第一筆成本。
causeEn: The invasion of AD 43 only makes sense if three threads are followed at once. The first is the condition of the empire's northern frontier: the legions stationed on the Rhine could not be taken away, and northern Gaul had only just been settled the year before, when the revolt of the chieftain Chnodomarius had been put down, so the empire needed a more secure western frontier. The second is a dispute over thrones in southern Britain itself: Verica, king of the Atrebates, had been driven out by his own subjects and fled to Gaul to appeal to Rome, and Vercassivellaunus, the father of Cogidumnus of the Regni, had fled to Rome even earlier and been installed there as a client king. On that basis the Romans could claim existing rights in southern Britain and intervene in the role of arbiter. The third is the emperor's own position: after the attack at Rouen in the spring of AD 43, Claudius needed a victory to consolidate the authority he had only just won, while freedmen like Narcissus and Pallas were themselves in need of military distinction. Dio records that the emperor's first demand was the return of the exiles and of property that had been carried off; Cassivellaunus refused, and the war began. On the economic level, conquest also meant control of the tin and lead of the south-west and of the trade routes between Britain and Gaul: a long-term return, of which the expedition was the first outlay.
impact: 四十三年的結果，不只是多了一個行省。卡穆羅杜努姆的殖民地、倫敦的永久據點、韋魯拉米烏姆等城鎮網、以及向西北延伸的軍用道路，把南不列顛改造成可徵稅、可徵兵、可調糧的行政區；銅礦、錫礦、鉛礦開採與沿海貿易被收歸帝國體系，隨後南不列顛的貴族與羅馬公民之間形成長達數個世紀的契約式關係：地方精英學會用拉丁文、進入行省議會、把自己的姓氏刻在羅馬式建築與墓碑上。硬實的代價也很快到來——被帝國扶植又遭帝國背叛的不列顛部族，在六十年與六十一年掀起的布狄卡之亂，規模遠超四十三年的抵抗，最後被鎮壓得極其殘酷，行省體制因此重整，附庸王國被逐步取消。也正因為南方已安，四十三年的戰果才讓北方的高地戰役得以進行：卡爾加庫斯在蒙斯格勞皮烏斯之戰的演說、阿格里科拉的推進，以及公元八十四年凱撒撤走北方軍團，標誌著征服的真正結束，哈德良長城則是一百二十二年才劃定的最終國界。這場戰爭最終改變的不列顛，是一個島的行政版圖，也是一個帝國的西界。
impactEn: The result of AD 43 was more than one more province. The colony at Camulodunum, the permanent base at Londinium, a network of towns such as Verulamium, and the military roads running north-west turned southern Britain into an administrative district that could be taxed, conscripted and provisioned; the working of the copper, tin and lead mines and the coastal trade were folded into the imperial system, and between the elites of southern Britain and the Roman citizen body there grew a contractual relationship lasting several centuries: local leaders learned Latin, sat in the provincial assembly, and had their names cut into Roman-style buildings and tombstones. The hard cost came quickly as well. The British tribes whom the empire had propped up and then betrayed rose in the revolt of Boudica in AD 60 and 61 on a scale far beyond the resistance of AD 43, and it was crushed with extreme brutality; the provincial system was reorganised in consequence, and the client kingdoms were abolished one by one. Precisely because the south had been settled, the harvest of AD 43 made the Highland campaigns possible at all: Calgacus's speech before Mons Graupius, the advance of Agricola, and the withdrawal of the northern legions by Caesar in AD 84 marked the true end of the conquest, while Hadrian's Wall, laid out in AD 122, was the final line of the frontier. What this war ultimately altered was not only the administrative map of an island but the western edge of an empire.
result: 就公元四十三至四十四年的戰役本身而言，結果是南方在政治上歸入帝國的秩序。卡西維拉努斯在倫敦與卡穆羅杜努姆一線重整兵馬、兩度求和，最終在皇帝抵島後到卡穆羅杜努姆投降；曼杜布拉基烏斯與科吉杜姆努斯留作附庸王，庫諾貝利努斯送出人質並納貢。不列顛南部此後二十年間維持相對平靜，直到布狄卡起義把這份平衡一次打碎。羅馬方面的收穫同樣具體：卡穆羅杜努姆殖民地建立並配駐守軍，倫敦與泰晤士河渡口被牢牢釘住，帝國在島上留駐第十瓦萊里亞·維克托里克斯等部隊，公元四十四年一月十七日皇帝在羅馬舉行盛大凱旋——由大象拉乘的戰車是自龐培以來首次，凱旋拱門也隨之立起。失敗同樣真實：倫敦一役的慘敗、卡穆羅杜努姆殖民地初期的被攻破與守軍覆沒、普勞提烏斯的追討戰，都說明這不是一場乾淨的勝利。征服並未因四十四年的投降而結束，北部要再打三十年，帝國真正的代價要到公元八十四年才付清。
resultEn: As far as the campaign of AD 43 and 44 is concerned, the outcome was the political incorporation of the south into the imperial order. Cassivellaunus re-raised his forces along the Thames and the road to Camulodunum and twice sued for terms, and finally surrendered at Camulodunum after the emperor reached the island; Mandubracius and Cogidumnus were left as client kings, and Cunobelinus sent hostages and paid tribute. Southern Britain enjoyed some twenty years of comparative quiet after that, until the revolt of Boudica broke the balance in a single stroke. The Roman gains were equally concrete: the colony at Camulodunum was founded and garrisoned, Londinium and the Thames crossing were nailed down for good, and the empire left troops on the island, including the Twentieth Valeria Victrix. On 17 January AD 44 the emperor celebrated a full triumph in Rome, with a chariot drawn by elephants for the first time since Pompey, and the triumphal arch was raised to match. The failures are just as real: the mauling on the Thames, the breaking of the early colony at Camulodunum and the loss of the troops stationed there, and Plautius's punitive expedition all show that this was not a clean victory. The conquest did not end with the surrender of AD 44; the north would take another thirty years, and the empire's true bill was not settled until AD 84.
